cues.text: Two of our classes.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Okay. What would you like to know?
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Well, I'm new to this area. So perhaps you could tell me something about the park first, please.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Of course. Altogether, the park covers 170 acres. That's 69 hectares. There are three main types of habitat. Wetland, grassland and woodland. The woods are well established and varied, with an oak plantation and other areas of mixed species.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: The wetland is quite varied too. The original farmland was dug up around 40 years ago to extract gravel. Once this work was completed, the gravel pits filled with water, forming the two large lakes. There are also several smaller ones, ponds and a stream that flows through the park.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Okay, so I suppose with these different habitats there's quite a variety of wildlife.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: There certainly is. A lot of different species of birds and insects, and also animals like deer and rabbits.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: And I understand you organize educational visits for school parties.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: That's right. We can organize a wide range of activities and adapt them to suit all ages.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Can you give me some examples of the activities?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well, one focus is on science, where we help children to discover and study plants, trees and insects. They also collect and analyse data about the things they see. Another focus is on geography. The park is a great environment to learn and practice reading a map, and using a compass to navigate around the park.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Do you do anything connected with history?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes, we do. For instance, the children can explore how the use of the land has changed over time. Then there's leisure and tourism.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: That focuses on your visitors, I would imagine.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes, mostly. The children find out about them, their requirements, the problems they may cause, and how we manage these. And another subject we cover is music. Here the children experiment with natural materials to create sounds and explore rhythm and tempo.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: That must be fun.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Most children really enjoy it
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: And of course all the activities are educational too. Learning outside the classroom encourages children to be creative and to explore and discover for themselves.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: I would imagine they get a sense of freedom that might not be a normal part of their lives.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: That's right. And very often the children discover that they can do things they didn't know they could do and they develop new skills. This gives them greater self -confidence.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: It sounds great. So what about the practical side of it? How much does it cost for a full day visit? We would expect to bring between 30 and 40 children.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: If there are over 30, it costs £4 .95 for each child who attends on the day. We invoice you afterwards, so you don't pay for children who can't come because of sickness, for example. There's no charge for leaders and other adults, as many as you want to bring.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: That sounds very fair. Well, thanks for all the information. I'll need to discuss it with my colleagues, and I hope to get back to you soon to make a booking.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: We'll look forward to hearing from you. Goodbye.
cues.speaker: WOMAN

cues.text: Goodbye, and thank you.
cues.speaker: MAN
